name: CPU Performance Mode
description: CPU and GPU governor tuning, Android battery saver, CPU frequency capping, and diagnostics: system CPU/RAM/temp, WebView dashboard responsiveness (with rolling p95/peak and renderer reload tracking), and top processes by CPU/RAM. No native code; every control is a root shell command over standard Linux cpufreq/devfreq sysfs nodes.
author: David Coulson

settings.title: GPU governor
settings.description: Only shown as effective if this panel exposes a GPU devfreq node.

settings.title: Android battery saver
settings.description: Toggles Android's own system Battery Saver, separate from the CPU/GPU governor.

settings.title: Max CPU frequency
settings.description: Caps every CPU core's top clock speed to this percentage of its own hardware maximum. 100% leaves the ceiling untouched.

settings.title: Min CPU frequency
settings.description: Raises every CPU core's floor clock speed to this percentage of its own hardware maximum, to reduce ramp-up lag. 0% leaves the floor at the kernel default. Best-effort: some panels silently hold a higher floor than this can lower, so results vary by hardware.

settings.title: Simulation mode
settings.description: Test the controls without touching hardware.
